L0: A procedure that changes an agent's available budget during a task to test how it verifies its work.
L1: A procedure that, after the first successful retrieval, changes either the remaining token budget or the tool-call quota; in distractor versions, it lowers the tool-call quota midway through the task. It is used for agentic tasks with chained browser or tool-use actions, rather than simple answer-extraction items.
L2: A procedure used in agentic tasks involving chained browser or tool-use actions, including distractor versions, rather than simple answer-extraction items. After the first successful retrieval, it changes either the remaining token budget or the tool-call quota; in distractor versions, it lowers the tool-call quota midway through the task. It produces and measures verification traces after that change, including their length, number of tool calls, and redundant page openings. Results are read by whether agents shorten those traces as quotas fall: high-performing agents do so, while lower-performing agents keep initiating tools until forced termination. Reduced redundant actions do not by themselves remove inappropriate reuse of recently successful action sequences, which can remain near its original rate. This quota-driven trace shortening is distinct from prior-session trace carryover, which affects session-carryover errors.
